summary:
I inventoried WinPoint's Settings app as it stands at checkout /home/robin/Documents/Codex/2026-11-01/chat/outputs/win11-gnome (branch claude/gnome-english-update). This was read-only: I edited nothing and did not touch the live session.

PAGE TREE (native/apps/settings/src/registry.rs PAGES, in navigation order; titles are nl/en)
- home: Startpagina/Home
- system: Systeem/System. Children: display (Beeldscherm/Display), sound (Geluid/Sound), notifications (Meldingen/Notifications), power (Energie en batterij/Power & battery), storage (Opslag/Storage), clipboard (Klembord/Clipboard), about (Info/About)
- bluetooth: Bluetooth en apparaten/Bluetooth & devices. It has no sub-pages, so there is no Mouse, Touchpad, Keyboard, Printers, Pen, Camera, AutoPlay or USB page.
- network: Netwerk en internet/Network & internet. Children: wifi (Wi-Fi), ethernet (Ethernet)
- personalization: Persoonlijke instellingen/Personalisation. Children: background (Achtergrond/Background), colors (Kleuren/Colours), themes (Thema’s/Themes), start (Start), taskbar (Taakbalk/Taskbar), desktopicons (Bureaubladpictogrammen/Desktop icons)
- apps: Apps. Children: installed (Geïnstalleerde apps/Installed apps), defaultapps (Standaard-apps/Default apps), startup (Opstarten/Startup)
- accounts: Accounts. No sub-pages.
- time: Tijd en taal/Time & language. Children: datetime (Datum en tijd/Date & time), language (Taal en regio/Language & region)
- accessibility: Toegankelijkheid/Accessibility. Children: textsize (Tekstgrootte/Text size), visualeffects (Visuele effecten/Visual effects), contrast (Contrastthema’s/Contrast themes)
- privacy: Privacy en beveiliging/Privacy & security. No sub-pages.
- update: Update en herstel/Update & recovery. Children: update-history (Updategeschiedenis/Update history), update-advanced (Geavanceerde opties/Advanced options)

Other registry facts:
- The search page id is "search". ALIASES maps ms-settings-style names (for example windowsupdate-history and night-light) to page ids.
- Compared with Windows 11 the nav lacks a Gaming entry, and there are no nested sub-pages under Bluetooth & devices, Accounts or Privacy & security.
- Installed GNOME panels: about, applications, background, bluetooth, color, datetime, display, keyboard, mouse, multitasking, network, notifications, online-accounts, power, printers, privacy, region, search, sharing, sound, system, ubuntu, universal-access, users, wacom, wellbeing, wifi, wwan (gnome-control-center 1:50.3-0ubuntu0.2).
- These panels have no WinPoint page or control at all: mouse, keyboard, printers, color, multitasking, online-accounts, search, sharing, wacom, wellbeing, wwan, ubuntu, users (except an info dialog), region (formats and input sources), the system sub-panels (remote desktop, secure shell, users), the universal-access content, and privacy (location, camera, microphone, screen lock, file history and trash, diagnostics, device security).

WHAT REALLY CHANGES GNOME TODAY
- Power: org.gnome.desktop.session idle-delay; org.gnome.settings-daemon.plugins.power idle-dim and sleep-inactive-{ac,battery}-{type,timeout}; the power-profiles-daemon ActiveProfile.
- Background: org.gnome.desktop.background picture-uri, picture-uri-dark, picture-options, primary-color, secondary-color, color-shading-type and picture-opacity. Written by the panel host's wallpaper.rs and recorded in gnome_look.
- Mode: org.gnome.desktop.interface color-scheme, gtk-theme and icon-theme, plus org.gnome.desktop.wm.preferences button-layout. Written by settings_effects.rs when theme.syncSystem is on (default true, no UI control) and recorded in gnome_look.
- Caption buttons: CSS blocks in ~/.config/gtk-3.0/gtk.css and ~/.config/gtk-4.0/gtk.css.
- Updates: com.ubuntu.update-notifier regular-auto-launch-interval.
- Files: ~/.config/mimeapps.list and xdg-terminals.list, ~/.config/autostart, and ~/.local/share/recently-used.xbel.
- System services:
  - BlueZ D-Bus with WinPoint's own temporary agent.
  - NetworkManager: reads over D-Bus, writes through nmcli.
  - rfkill.
  - wpctl (PipeWire).
  - logind: SetBrightness, plus systemctl and loginctl for the power actions.
  - PackageKit, and pkexec with WinPoint's own polkit policy for Ubuntu release prompts.

READ-ONLY, FAKE OR HYPRLAND-ONLY ON GNOME
- Display: scale, resolution and refresh rate are greyed. display.list reads Mutter DisplayConfig.GetCurrentState, and display.set is Hyprland only. Arrangement, Identify and the 15 s keep dialog only appear on Hyprland.
- Night light: system.nightLight.set uses hyprsunset (Hyprland only), so the page shows an unavailable card and the settings.json nightLight.* keys go unused.
- Clipboard history: clipboard.list returns supported:false on GNOME, so the buttons are disabled.
- Rename this PC, Your info and Sign-in options only open dialogs that point to Ubuntu's Settings app.
- Date & time: the "Set time automatically" switch and the time zone dropdown are disabled and only show timedatectl's values.
- Contrast themes is a notice saying it is not available yet. Nothing sets accessibility.highContrast.
- taskbar.widgets has no consumer; only the mini preview reads it.
- notifications.sounds has no consumer anywhere.

WinPoint-only (they never touch GNOME's equivalent key): transparency, accent colour (GNOME accent-color is read but never written), text size (not text-scaling-factor), animations (not enable-animations), 24-hour clock (not clock-format), first day of week, display language (not the system locale), privacy.recentFiles (not remember-recent-files), and notifications showToasts and dnd (not show-banners).

ARCHITECTURE A NEW PAGE MUST FOLLOW
1. Register the page:
   - Add an entry to registry.rs PAGES: id, parent, an icon from kit glyph_data NAMES (mouse, keyboard, print, camera, mic, gamepad and so on all exist), title, description and keywords, each as an nl/en pair.
   - Add any ALIASES.
   - Add `pub const PAGES: &[(&str, Builder)]` and `pub const CSS` in a pages/*.rs module, then add the module to MODULES and MODULE_CSS in pages/mod.rs.
   - A new top-level category needs its own drawing in navicons.rs (otherwise it gets System's) and a place in PAGES order.
   - The parent page lists its sub-pages itself with common::link_card(&p, id), as in the system.rs id loop.
2. Build the page:
   - A builder is `fn(Page) -> PageFuture`: start every p.call() first, then await them, check p.alive(), and return a Vec<gtk::Widget>.
   - p.get, p.run and p.run_with add the error toast and the dry-run toast. Also available: p.on(event prefix), p.on_settings, p.timeout, p.interval, p.on_cleanup, p.go, p.go_with, p.refresh, p.take_param.
3. Controls:
   - From kit::controls: SettingsGroup, SettingsCard (new or clickable with a Chevron), SettingsExpander, ToggleSwitch, Dropdown/DropdownOption, Slider (connect_changed for live updates, connect_committed for the final value, set_value_visible(false)), RadioGroup, checkbox and checkbox_desc, ColorSwatches, InfoBar, Dialog and confirm, Toast, MenuItem, SearchBox, ProgressBar/ProgressRing, Pivot/Segmented, number_box, text_box.
   - From common.rs: setting_toggle, setting_dropdown, toggle_card and dropdown_card (bound to settings.json), link_card and link_card_with, notice and unavailable_card, sized, value_label, slot and set_slot, hero, hero_tile, UsageBar, kbd, card_extra.
   - Also widgets::{Wrap, Clamp, AutoGrid}, background::FillGrid, preview::{DesktopPreview, DeviceArt} and colorpicker::pick_color.
   - Texts are kit::t(nl, en) in Windows 11 nl-NL wording with no em-dashes. A language switch rebuilds the page.
4. settings.json:
   - Lives at ~/.config/win11-gnome/settings.json. Write with kit ctx settings.set {path, value} or settings.patch {patch}.
   - host/src/settings.rs validates each value by type against host/src/settings-defaults.json. Unknown keys are kept, so add new keys to the defaults to get type checking.
   - Changes reach every app as the settings.changed SSE event.
   - Operating-system side effects only happen in settings_effects.rs (theme.*) and wallpaper.rs (wallpaper.*).
5. Host calls:
   - The kit starts a `win11-app --http-only` backend child and calls POST /api/call/<method> with a token. The SSE stream is /api/events.
   - Every method must be listed in host/src/api-methods.json (otherwise unknown_method). Its "dangerous" flag adds the dryRun envelope, and the service itself must skip the write when ctx.dry_run.
   - host/src/services/mod.rs Services::call dispatches by prefix (system., display., update., and so on) to the service's METHODS list and match.
   - Errors are ApiError::tr(code, lang, key) with nl/en strings, for example services/system/strings.json.
   - Events go out with ctx.emit("system.<domain>.changed", value). System::publish only sends when the value changed, and a dirty-domain set is filled by GSettings or D-Bus signals.
6. The existing pattern for GSettings is host/src/services/system/energy.rs:
   - gio::SettingsSchemaSource::default().lookup(id, true). A missing schema means {available:false}.
   - The snapshot is {available, writable via is_writable for lockdown, value}, with a type check on value_type.
   - write() checks type, range_check and is_writable first, then does delay, set_value, apply and Settings::sync, and reads the value back.
   - Patch::parse accepts exactly one key per call.
   - watch() uses connect_changed and connect_writable_changed on the service's GLib context and emits system.power.settings.changed.
   - A new system.input.get/set (mouse, touchpad, keyboard), system.nightLight on org.gnome.settings-daemon.plugins.color, or a whitelisted gsettings.get/set should copy this pattern.
   - Preference keys are shared with GNOME exactly as GNOME Settings writes them, with no gnome_look. Only keys that are part of WinPoint's look go through gnome_look::note, so `win11-app --gnome-look` restores GNOME's values in non-WinPoint sessions. That is the existing guarantee that WinPoint does not break the normal GNOME/Ubuntu session.
7. System writes go through polkit. Either use daemons that already check polkit (NetworkManager, BlueZ, logind, power-profiles-daemon, and also timedated, hostnamed, localed and AccountsService, which GNOME Settings uses but WinPoint does not yet call), or follow the services/update/admin.rs pattern: pkexec with a root-owned trusted helper and an own .policy in host/data, installed by scripts/install-system.py.
8. Anything only gnome-shell can do goes over the extension bridge io.github.win11shell.GnomeBridge Call(method, json) (host/src/gnome.rs, extension/*Bridge.js).

Existing services to extend:
- system/audio.rs (wpctl): sources, balance.
- system/energy.rs: power-button-action, ambient-enabled, show-battery-percentage, power-saver-profile-on-low-battery.
- display.rs (Mutter DisplayConfig): add ApplyMonitorsConfig.
- system/network.rs: VPN, proxy, hotspot.
- system/bluetooth.rs: adapter alias and discoverable.
- system/info.rs: hostnamed.
- apps/defaults.rs: mime types, removable media.
- sysmon/startup.rs.
- update/options.rs: another GSettings writer.
- notifications.rs and extension/notificationsBridge.js.

items.function: Page builder contract
items.backing: fn(Page) -> PageFuture; start p.call()s first then await (parallel); `if !p.alive() { return vec![] }`; return Vec<gtk::Widget> of SettingsGroups/cards; p.run/run_with show the error and dry-run toasts; p.on(prefix), p.on_settings, p.timeout/interval/on_cleanup stop with the page
items.notes: Documented in native/apps/settings/src/pages/mod.rs module doc.

items.function: settings.json controls

items.notes: OS side effects only via host/src/settings_effects.rs (theme.*) and wallpaper.rs (wallpaper.*).

items.function: New host method
items.backing: Add to host/src/api-methods.json {name, dangerous, doc} (unknown_method otherwise; dangerous adds the dryRun envelope); route by prefix in host/src/services/mod.rs Services::call; the service's METHODS list + match; skip writes when ctx.dry_run; ApiError::tr(code, lang, key) with nl/en strings (services/system/strings.json); emit ctx.emit('system.<domain>.changed', v)
items.notes: Transport: kit/src/backend.rs HTTP POST /api/call/<method> + SSE /api/events to a win11-app --http-only child.

items.function: Exposing GSettings keys (template)
items.backing: host/src/services/system/energy.rs: SettingsSchemaSource::default().lookup(id, true) (missing -> available:false); snapshot {available, writable: is_writable, value} with a value_type check; write(): type + range_check + is_writable, then delay/set_value/apply/Settings::sync and read back; Patch::parse one key per call; watch(): connect_changed + connect_writable_changed marks the domain dirty, then System::publish emits only on change
items.notes: Use for mouse/touchpad/keyboard (org.gnome.desktop.peripherals.*), night light (org.gnome.settings-daemon.plugins.color), a11y, privacy, interface keys. Preference keys are shared with GNOME and written as GNOME Settings writes them (no gnome_look::note). Only WinPoint-look keys go through gnome_look::note, so --gnome-look restores them in GNOME/Ubuntu sessions.

items.function: System writes through polkit
items.backing: Prefer system daemons that check polkit themselves (NetworkManager/nmcli, BlueZ, logind, power-profiles-daemon; also hostnamed, timedated, localed, AccountsService, which WinPoint does not call yet). Otherwise follow host/src/services/update/admin.rs: pkexec + root-owned trusted helper in /usr/libexec/win11-gnome + own .policy in host/data, installed by scripts/install-system.py; map exit 126/127
items.notes: GNOME Shell's polkit agent shows the password dialog.

items.function: GNOME Shell bridge
items.backing: io.github.win11shell.GnomeBridge Call(method, json) / Event signal (host/src/gnome.rs, kit/src/gnome.rs, extension/*Bridge.js); extension schema org.gnome.shell.extensions.win11-gnome (task-manager, task-view, *-restore keybindings)
items.notes: For things only gnome-shell can do (notification banners, windows, blur).
